cases.sentence: Петя при выезде из Москвы, оставив своих родных, присоединился к своему полку и скоро после этого был взят ординарцем к генералу, командовавшему ___.
cases.explain: «большим отрядом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Pétya, having left his people after their departure from Moscow, joined his regiment and was soon taken as orderly by a general commanding a large guerrilla detachment. From the time he received his commission, and especially since he had joined the active army and taken part in the battle of Vyázma, Pétya had been in a constant state of blissful excitement at being grown-up and in a perpetual ecstatic hurry not to miss any chance to do something really heroic. He was highly delighted with what he saw and experienced in the army, but at the same time it always seemed to him that the really heroic exploits were being performed just where he did not happen to be. And he was always in a hurry to get where he was not.

cases.sentence: В полутьме виднелись лошади в седлах, казаки, гусары, прилаживавшие шалашики на поляне и (чтобы не видели дыма французы) разводившие красневший огонь в ___.
cases.explain: «лесном овраге» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: It was already growing dusk when Denísov, Pétya, and the esaul rode up to the watchhouse. In the twilight saddled horses could be seen, and Cossacks and hussars who had rigged up rough shelters in the glade and were kindling glowing fires in a hollow of the forest where the French could not see the smoke. In the passage of the small watchhouse a Cossack with sleeves rolled up was chopping some mutton. In the room three officers of Denísov’s band were converting a door into a tabletop. Pétya took off his wet clothes, gave them to be dried, and at once began helping the officers to fix up the dinner table.

cases.sentence: На столе была водка, ром в фляжке, ___ и жареная баранина с солью.
cases.explain: «белый хлеб» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: In ten minutes the table was ready and a napkin spread on it. On the table were vodka, a flask of rum, white bread, roast mutton, and salt.

cases.sentence: Он стал вспоминать, не сделал ли он еще ___.
cases.explain: «каких-нибудь глупостей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: He tried to remember whether he had not done anything else that was foolish. And running over the events of the day he remembered the French drummer boy. “It’s capital for us here, but what of him? Where have they put him? Have they fed him? Haven’t they hurt his feelings?” he thought. But having caught himself saying too much about the flints, he was now afraid to speak out.

cases.sentence: «Спросить бы можно?» думал он, «да скажут: ___ и мальчика пожалел.
cases.explain: «сам мальчик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I might ask,” he thought, “but they’ll say: ‘He’s a boy himself and so he pities the boy.’ I’ll show them tomorrow whether I’m a boy. Will it seem odd if I ask?” Pétya thought. “Well, never mind!” and immediately, blushing and looking anxiously at the officers to see if they appeared ironical, he said:

cases.sentence: — Да, ___, — сказал Денисов, видимо не найдя ничего стыдного в этом напоминании.
cases.explain: «жалкий мальчишка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, he’s a poor little fellow,” said Denísov, who evidently saw nothing shameful in this reminder. “Call him in. His name is Vincent Bosse. Have him fetched.”

cases.explain: «Жалкий мальчишка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, yes, call him. A poor little fellow,” Denísov repeated.

cases.sentence: В обеих переделках это напоминание о весне сходилось с представлением о ___.
cases.explain: «молоденьком мальчике» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Vincent, the boy’s name, had already been changed by the Cossacks into Vesénny (vernal) and into Vesénya by the peasants and soldiers. In both these adaptations the reference to spring (vesná) matched the impression made by the young lad.

cases.sentence: — Merci, monsieur,[971] Благодарю, господин, — отвечал барабанщик дрожащим почти ___ и стал обтирать о порог свои грязные ноги.
cases.explain: «детским голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Merci, monsieur,”119 said the drummer boy in a trembling almost childish voice, and he began scraping his dirty feet on the threshold. There were many things Pétya wanted to say to the drummer boy, but did not dare to. He stood irresolutely beside him in the passage. Then in the darkness he took the boy’s hand and pressed it.

cases.translation: “Come in, come in!” he repeated in a gentle whisper. “Oh, what can I do for him?” he thought, and opening the door he let the boy pass in first.
